data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'Haros' meaning mountain and 'Elda' meaning ruler or goddess. Harelda was a name given to the goddess of childbirth and fertility in ancient Greece. The name Harelda carries the meaning “Ruler of the mountain” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Harelda usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler of the mountain and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength, protection, and divine guidance.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Harelda total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

Harelda was a goddess, symbolizing the power and strength of a mountain and the nurturing and life-giving capacities of a goddess. She was a deity of childbirth, representing the transformative power of nature in bringing new life into the world.
